name: Deepvein Mining Integrated Tunnel Suit Mk-6
description:
Gunmetal grey full-coverage tunnel suit with articulated knee and elbow reinforcement plates in battered orange. The outer shell is abrasion-resistant ripstop carbide-weave with sealed seams throughout. Integrated lighting strips run along the shoulders and forearms — low-power bioluminescent fallback strips beneath the primary LEDs ensure visibility even if power fails underground. Dust filters are built into the collar as a pull-up face seal.

The suit's back panel has a structured channel running spine-to-hip that accommodates spinal rigs and exoskeleton attachment rails. Tail-compatible versions exist as a Mk-6G variant with a reinforced rear gusset. Most suits show heavy scarring from rock contact along the shoulders and knees — miners consider a clean suit a sign of inexperience.
functionality: Abrasion-rated for continuous rock-face contact. Dual lighting system — primary LED with 12-hour battery, secondary bioluminescent strips rated 6 hours passive. Integrated dust-filter collar seal rated P100 equivalent. Spinal rig channel and exoskeleton rail attachment points at rear. Sealed seams resist fine particulate infiltration. Emergency reflective patches on back and knees.
what_it_says: You go into the ground and you come back out — and the suit proves how many times you've done it.
manufacturer: Deepvein Equipment Co. (Tier 1-2 industrial supplier, semi-licensed)
story_hooks: A mining crew's Mk-6 suits are all showing bioluminescent strip failure simultaneously — someone has been exposing them to a compound that degrades the bio-substrate, and the next deep shift has no backup lighting.
A veteran miner's suit has a carved tally on the left forearm plate — 847 marks — and she refuses to say what they count.
A sealed-off tunnel section beneath the Shelf contains a cache of Mk-6 suits still occupied, arranged deliberately, and someone has been keeping the area clear of salvagers for years.
related_entities: TESSERA CORPONATION Aegis CorpSec Hardened Security BCI

physical_description.visual_profile: A utilitarian full-body tunnel suit with industrial armor plating — gunmetal grey base with battered orange reinforcement at joints creates a worker's aesthetic of hard use and survival. The silhouette is squared-off and functional, designed for movement in cramped spaces rather than style. Glowing accent strips along shoulders and forearms give an eerie, safety-conscious presence in darkness.
physical_description.fit: Compression-cut through the torso with articulated joints at knees and elbows. Tapered at wrists and ankles for seal integrity. Back panel is structured and rigid to accept exoskeleton rails — not a relaxed fit, but engineered for load-bearing.
physical_description.primary_material: Carbide-weave ripstop outer shell with sealed seams. Inner lining is moisture-wicking synth-blend. Orange reinforcement plates are impact-molded polymer composite over ballistic mesh.
physical_description.texture: Outer surface is slightly dimpled from carbide treatment — rough to touch, designed for grip and abrasion resistance. Reinforcement plates show deep scoring and burnished edges from rock contact. Bioluminescent strips have a subtle waxy texture under the gloss.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal grey primary with oxidized charcoal undertones. Battered orange reinforcement plates at elbows, knees, and collar — the orange is faded and chipped, showing bare polymer beneath. Dark grey seams. Faint green glow from dormant bioluminescent strips.
physical_description.closures: Full-length magnetic snap front closure with redundant friction-fit collar seal. Wrist and ankle cuffs are compression-locked with micro-velcro secondary hold. Rear spinal rail has indexed quick-release clips for rig attachment.
distinctive_features: Dual-layer lighting system: primary LEDs in shoulders/forearms with bioluminescent fallback strips for power-loss situations
Integrated dust filter collar (pull-up face seal design)
Structured spinal channel running neck-to-hip with exoskeleton attachment rails
Heavy scarring and abrasion marks across shoulders, knees, and forearms from rock contact
Tail-compatible Mk-6G variant option with reinforced rear panel
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 2-3 industrial. Legitimate equipment from a semi-licensed supplier, not luxury but not salvage. Shows this wearer has steady contract work.
physical_description.cultural_context: The wearer is a professional tunnel miner or deepvein extraction worker. The heavy scarring is a badge of experience — a pristine suit signals inexperience or desk duty. This is working-class gear worn in the deep dark places beneath the GLMZ.
physical_description.condition_typical: Heavily weathered and scarred. Dust and mineral residue built into seams. Orange plating dulled and chipped. Likely repaired multiple times at stress points. A 'broken-in' suit is a trusted suit.
